text: Vendor master: the record of every external party an organization pays — and the one master domain that sits closest to financial fraud controls.

A vendor record carries a unique ID, legal name and tax ID, remittance versus physical address, banking details, payment terms, and status. Banking and payment data is why vendor master sits closer to financial controls than other master domains.

Duplicate vendor fraud: someone creates a second record for a real supplier with different banking details, then redirects a payment there. Strict duplicate checking and change control on bank details is the primary defense — and sanctions screening against watch lists happens right at record creation.

Vendor onboarding collects and verifies a new supplier's information — tax ID, banking, sanctions screening — before the record goes live for purchasing. Treating that as a gate, not something any employee can bypass ad hoc, is what makes the fraud controls actually work.

Not every vendor needs the same scrutiny. A strategic supplier gets a dedicated owner and performance scorecards; a one-time office-supply vendor gets a lighter record. The segment itself should live in the master data so downstream workflows apply different rules automatically.
Next lesson: employee and location master — the internal-facing domains that round out the picture before we get to hierarchies in general.
